title.rendered: UNIOSUN students deserve justice after military invasion — Spokesperson

content.rendered:
Public Relations Officer of Osun State University, Osogbo, Mr Ademola Adesoji, tells BIODUN BUSARI about the alleged assault on students by a group of military personnel who invaded their off-campus hostels

Could you share an insight into the incident involving your students and some military personnel?

The incident occurred in the Shasha/Oke Baale area of Osogbo, Osun State, where a significant number of our students reside in privately owned off-campus hostels. The neighbourhood is widely recognised as a student community due to its proximity to the university. It is also located close to the Nigerian Army Depot, where military recruits undergo training. Both facilities are situated within the same general area.

Could you briefly explain the Army Depot in that vicinity?

The Nigerian Army Depot in Oke Baale serves as a training facility for military recruits. It is one of the country’s recognised centres for the training and development of personnel of the Nigerian Army.

What really happened in the community?

Based on reports received by the university and accounts provided by affected students and other witnesses, the incident occurred late at night when some individuals identified as military personnel allegedly entered several privately owned student hostels in the area.

During the incident, some students and security personnel attached to the hostels were reportedly assaulted, while several students alleged that they were subjected to various forms of physical and emotional abuse. These accounts formed the basis of the university’s decision to intervene promptly and seek appropriate action from the relevant authorities.

How many soldiers were involved?

At this stage, the university is unable to verify the exact number of personnel involved. Given the nature of the incident and the circumstances under which it reportedly occurred, it would be inappropriate to speculate. We consider it the responsibility of the appropriate investigative authorities to establish the facts.

Has anything like this happened before?

To the best of the university’s knowledge, this is the first incident of this nature involving our students in that community. The hostels concerned are privately owned, and we have not received reports of a similar occurrence in the past.

Have there been previous altercations or disputes between the students and the soldiers?

The university is not aware of any previous incidents or recurring disputes between our students and personnel from the Army Depot. The community has historically remained peaceful, and we have no official records indicating any pattern of conflict.

How many students were assaulted by the soldiers?

More than 30 students were directly affected by the incident to varying degrees. While some sustained physical injuries, others experienced psychological and emotional trauma.

The exact number remains subject to ongoing documentation and verification, as the university is ensuring that every affected student is properly accounted for and receives the necessary support.

How have their parents taken the matter?

Naturally, the incident has generated considerable concern among parents and guardians. Many have reached out to the university to express their anxiety and seek assurances regarding the safety and well-being of their children.

The university understands these concerns and has maintained open communication with parents, updating them on the measures being taken to support the affected students and engage the relevant authorities.

We appreciate the confidence parents continue to repose in the institution and remain committed to providing a safe, secure, and conducive learning environment for all our students while pursuing the matter through appropriate and lawful channels.

How have the school authorities addressed the situation?

Immediately after the reports came to the university’s attention, the management activated its crisis response mechanism. The university publicly condemned the incident, expressed concern for the safety and welfare of its students, and formally engaged the relevant authorities.

The Vice-Chancellor also constituted a high-powered committee to document the allegations, support the affected students and make appropriate recommendations.

The university has prioritised the physical, emotional and psychological well-being of the affected students by providing access to medical care and counselling services. We remain committed to ensuring that every affected student receives the necessary support while due process takes its course.

What was the Army’s response to this?

The Nigerian Army publicly acknowledged the reports and announced that it had commenced an internal investigation into the allegations. Subsequently, an invitation was extended to affected persons to provide information.

The university’s position has been that any engagement involving our students should be conducted in a manner that guarantees their safety, protects their rights and inspires confidence in the investigative process.

Consequently, the university has continued to engage the appropriate authorities to ensure that any investigation is conducted in a fair, transparent and victim-sensitive manner.

In what way have civil rights groups shown interest in helping?

A number of civil society organisations and human rights groups have expressed concern over the incident and have indicated their willingness to support efforts aimed at ensuring justice and protecting the rights of the affected students.

We are also aware that the Nigerian Bar Association, Osogbo Branch, has indicated its readiness to provide legal support to affected students should the need arise.

We appreciate the interest of these organisations and remain committed to working with all relevant stakeholders within the law to resolve the matter fairly, responsibly, and in the best interests of justice.
